# CSIT6000V (L1) - Advanced AI Computing and Systems Assignment 1: MPI Programming Submission deadline: October 22, 2026, 23:59 ### I. General Notes 1. This assignment counts for 10 points. 2. This is an individual assignment. You may discuss the assignment with others and consult online resources, but the submitted implementation must be your own work. Academic integrity rules of the course apply. 3. Add your name, student ID, and email in comments at the beginning of your source file. 4. Submit your assignment through Canvas before the deadline. 5. All submissions will be compiled and tested uniformly in the official course computing environment. Students are strongly encouraged to use the provided testing workflow before submission. 6. Please direct assignment-related questions to dzhangce@connect.ust.hk. ### II. Problem Description This assignment focuses on the MPI parallelization of a General Matrix-Matrix Multiplication (GEMM) operator. Given $$ A\in\mathbb{R}^{M\times K} $$ and $$ B\in\mathbb{R}^{K\times N}, $$ GEMM computes $$ C=A\times B,\qquad C\in\mathbb{R}^{M\times N}, $$ where $$ C_{i j}=\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}A_{i k}B_{k j}. $$ In the sequential version, GEMM is computed by a single process. In this assignment, you will parallelize GEMM using a simple 1D row partitioning strategy. Matrix A is divided by rows among MPI processes, while every MPI process uses the complete matrix B. Each process computes its assigned rows of C, and the local results are finally gathered to Process 0.
RankRank 0Rank 1Rank 2 / ...
$ A_{{0}} $$ A_{{1}} $$ A_{{2}}, ... $
$ \downarrow $$ \downarrow $$ \downarrow $
$ A_{{0}} \times B $$ A_{{1}} \times B $$ A_{{2}} \times B, ... $
$ \downarrow $$ \downarrow $$ \downarrow $
$ C_{{0}} $$ C_{{1}} $$ C_{{2}}, ... $
Gather to Process 0:$ C = [C_{{0}}; C_{{1}}; C_{{2}}; ...] $

### III. Sequential Algorithm

Algorithm 1: GEMM (sequential)

Input:
matrix A of size $M \times K$
matrix B of size $K \times N$

1. Procedure GEMM(A, B, M, K, N):
2. initialize $C[M][N]$ to zero
3. for i from 0 to $M - 1$ do:
4. for j from 0 to $N - 1$ do:
5. $C_{ij} = 0$
6. for k from 0 to $K - 1$ do:
7. $C_{ij} = C_{ij} + A_{ik}B_{kj}$
8. end for
9. end for
10. end for
11. return C
12. end procedure

### IV. Your Implementation Task

The code skeleton "gemm_mpi.c" is provided.

Your task is to complete the missing code in the designated section of the main function.

1. Scatter the rows of matrix A to the MPI processes and make matrix B available to every MPI process.

2. Perform the local GEMM computation in each process:

 $$ l o c a l\_{C}=l o c a l\_{A}\times B. $$ 

3. Gather all local result blocks to Process 0 and assemble them into the complete output matrix C in the correct row order.

## Notes:

### 1. Row Partitioning

For all provided and evaluation test cases, the number of rows $M$ will be divisible by the number of MPI processes $P$:

 $$ M\bmod P=0. $$ 

Therefore, every MPI process receives the same number of rows of matrix A.

### 2. A typical implementation may use

## MPI_Bcast, MPI_Scatter, and MPI_Gather

Equivalent MPI communication methods that correctly implement the required parallel computation may also be used.

3. The sequential GEMM implementation is provided for reference and result comparison.

4. For more information about MPI APIs, refer to the MPI documentation introduced in the tutorial.

Do not submit a ZIP archive, executable file, output file, testing log, screenshot, or any additional files.

Running tcloud submit does not replace the final Canvas submission.

### 2. Evaluation

Programs will be evaluated using multiple matrix dimensions and valid MPI process counts.

The evaluation datasets may differ from the public test datasets.

Evaluation focuses on correctness and correct MPI-based parallel execution.

Performance and parallel speedup will not be evaluated.

### 3. Grading rubric

## • 10 points

The program successfully passes the required multi-process MPI executions and produces correct results for all evaluation test cases.

## • 5 points

The program produces correct results in single-process execution, but does not successfully pass the required multi-process MPI evaluation.

## • 0 points

The program fails to compile, fails to execute correctly, or produces incorrect results.

No performance or speedup measurement is included in the grading.
